variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: defparameter and defvar define global (dynamic) variables. let creates local lexical bindings.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
42                   ; integer
3.14                 ; float
5/2                  ; ratio
#c(1 2)              ; complex number
"Hello"              ; string
#\A                  ; character
'symbol              ; symbol
'(1 2 3)             ; list
#(1 2 3)             ; vector
t                    ; boolean true
nil                  ; boolean false / empty list
data_types.notes: Common Lisp has a rich set of built-in data types including ratios, complex numbers, and multi-dimensional arrays.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
(+ 1 2 3)    ; => 6
(- 10 4)     ; => 6
(* 2 3)      ; => 6
(/ 10 2)     ; => 5

(= 1 1)      ; Numeric equality
(equal "a" "a") ; Structural equality
(eq 'a 'a)   ; Identity equality

(and t nil)  ; => nil
(or nil t)   ; => t
(not t)      ; => nil
operators.notes: Operators are just regular functions in prefix notation. Many numeric functions accept multiple arguments.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: if takes a condition, a then-form, and an optional else-form. cond is used for multi-way branching (like switch/else-if).

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
(dotimes (i 10)
  (print i))

(loop for i from 1 to 10
      do (print i))

(loop for x in '(a b c)
      collect (list x x))
for_loop.notes: The loop macro provides a powerful domain-specific language for iteration. dotimes is a simpler macro for iterating a fixed number of times.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
(let ((x 0))
  (loop while (< x 10)
        do (print x)
           (incf x)))

;; Or using do
(do ((x 0 (1+ x)))
    ((>= x 10))
  (print x))
while_loop.notes: while loops can be written using the loop macro. The do macro provides a more traditional Lisp iteration construct.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
(defun add (a b)
  "Adds two numbers."
  (+ a b))

;; Anonymous function (lambda)
(lambda (x) (* x x))

;; Calling a lambda
(funcall #'(lambda (x) (* x x)) 5)

;; Optional and keyword arguments
(defun greet (name &optional (greeting "Hello") &key (punctuation "!"))
  (format nil "~a, ~a~a" greeting name punctuation))
functions.notes: defun creates named functions. lambda creates anonymous functions. Common Lisp supports optional, rest, and keyword arguments.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
;; Creating a 1D array (vector)
(make-array 5 :initial-element 0)
#(1 2 3 4 5) ; Literal syntax

;; Accessing and modifying
(defparameter *v* (make-array 3 :initial-element 0))
(aref *v* 0)           ; => 0
(setf (aref *v* 0) 42) ; Modifies the array
arrays.notes: make-array creates arrays of any dimension. aref accesses elements, and setf combined with aref modifies them.

maps.title: Maps (Hash Tables)
maps.code:
(defparameter *ht* (make-hash-table :test 'equal))

;; Setting values
(setf (gethash "key" *ht*) "value")

;; Getting values
(gethash "key" *ht*) ; Returns two values: value and boolean presence

;; Removing values
(remhash "key" *ht*)
maps.notes: Hash tables are the standard associative data structure. :test determines the equality function used for keys (default is eql).

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
(handler-case (/ 1 0)
  (division-by-zero (c)
    (format t "Caught error: ~a~%" c)
    0)
  (error (c)
    (print "Caught some other error")))

;; Signaling an error
(error "Something went wrong")
error_handling.notes: Common Lisp has a powerful condition system. handler-case is used like try/catch. You can also use restarts for more advanced error recovery.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
;; Single-line comment in Lisp
#|
 Multi-line block comment
|#
(defun add (a b)
  "Documentation string for function"
  (+ a b))
comments.notes: Common Lisp uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
(def x 42)          ; Integer
(def pi 3.14159)    ; Float
(def ratio 1/3)     ; Exact rational ratio
(def hex #xFF)      ; Hexadecimal
numbers.notes: Common Lisp supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: Common Lisp treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Common Lisp performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.code:
(def s "Hello, World!")
(def char-val (char s 0))
(def multi "Line 1
Line 2")
strings.notes: Common Lisp represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Common Lisp formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Common Lisp, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Common Lisp constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.notes: Common Lisp achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Common Lisp emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Common Lisp are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Common Lisp uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Common Lisp provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Common Lisp isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
